question:
For all integers \(n \ge 9,\) the value of

\[\frac{(n + 2)! - (n + 1)!}{n!}\]

is always which of the following?
solution:
The two factorials in the numerator share a common factor, which lets us simplify without calculating either factorial.

Using \((n+2)!=(n+2)(n+1)!\), we get
\[
\frac{(n+2)!-(n+1)!}{n!}
=\frac{(n+1)!\bigl((n+2)-1\bigr)}{n!}
=\frac{(n+1)!(n+1)}{n!}.
\]
Now \((n+1)!=(n+1)n!\), and \(n!\ne0\) for every allowed \(n\). Canceling gives
\[
\frac{(n+1)n!(n+1)}{n!}=(n+1)^2.
\]
Since \(n+1\) is an integer, the expression is always a perfect square, choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
